updates.summary: A count of spells cast is tested `>= 1`, as every other event history count is.
updates.evidence: In the allowed population of the pinned export, every other event history count tested for at least one occurrence uses `>= 1` (83 of them count spells cast). These five Spell Cast tests alone use `> 0`. Patrician's Scorn, Soul Reap and Talara's Battalion read Dream Thief's wording, "if you've cast another <color> spell this turn", with `>= 1`.

changes.face: I Bask in Your Silent Awe

updates.summary: One explicitly defined X is captured once before drawing and losing life, including kinded counter counts.
updates.evidence: Bone Devourer says "you draw X cards and you lose X life, where X is the number of +1/+1 counters on it". Necropotence Avatar says "put a death counter on Necropotence Avatar. You draw X cards and you lose X life, where X is the number of death counters on Necropotence Avatar". Both uses name the same defined quantity; the latter definition is evaluated after counter placement. The pinned reference already uses BindValue followed by two BoundValue reads for Parting Thoughts (all counters on the destroyed target) and Savanti Romero, Time's Exile (all counters on the source after counter placement). These two kinded counts use duplicate inline CountCounters operands. Normalize them to that existing shared-X form; retain the reference's object identity (EventSubject for Bone Devourer, Source for Necropotence Avatar), counter kind, CurrentOrLastKnown, the preceding placement and original action result IDs. No source/holder alias, AST schema change or equality exception is introduced. See docs/grammar-simplification-20261113.md.

updates.summary: Suspect uses KeywordEach for singleton objects and optional target populations, as it already does for sets.
updates.evidence: The allowed pinned export has 13 scalar Keyword{action:Suspect{object}} operations and seven KeywordEach{action:Suspect,objects} operations for the same keyword action. Barbed Servitor, Frantic Scapegoat and Person of Interest already suspect one object with KeywordEach; Convenient Target and Incriminating Impetus do so for the attached creature. The scalar form is the same action on One(object), with its actor unchanged. An up-to-one target denotes its entire announced Targets(slot) population, including zero objects, rather than selecting index zero. Preserve Source, EventSubject, moved-object Result references, target slots and all result identities. The owned canonical contract normalizes the same forms for edited/synthesized IR and preserves their typed ID provenance. See docs/grammar-simplification-20261113.md.

updates.summary: An explicit look-at-top-X definition is captured once for later selections or comparisons, as on Keldon Flamesage.
updates.evidence: Emergent Woodwurm says "look at the top X cards of your library, where X is its power" and then permits a permanent card "with mana value X or less". Its own and Backup-granted attack triggers share one definition in their respective ability-holder scopes. Kiora, Sovereign of the Deep says X is the triggering spell's mana value and permits a spell with mana value less than X. Thassa's Oracle defines X as devotion before looking and reordering, then compares that same X to the remaining library count. The pinned reference repeats ObjectProperty or CountManaSymbols at these later uses, while Keldon Flamesage already uses one BindValue and two BoundValue reads for the analogous look and mana-value selection. Normalize these four programs to one capture immediately before LookAt; preserve each original definition (EventSubject, property, information policy or devotion population), all original action/result IDs, Group structure, optional choices and reordering/cast operands. Allocate only a fresh definition result. The library-count operand of Thassa's later comparison remains live, evaluated after reordering. No Source/holder alias, global live-value equivalence, AST schema change or scorer exception is introduced. See docs/grammar-simplification-20261113.md.

updates.summary: A current battlefield Zone population does not repeat its own InZone(Battlefield) filter.
updates.evidence: Audit of the immutable allowed population found 22 sites on 22 faces with Matching{objects:Zone{scope:Shared(Battlefield),...},filter:InZone(Shared(Battlefield))}. The inner population consists only of current battlefield objects, so that outer membership test cannot remove an object. Other battlefield counts already use the Zone directly. ED-E, Lonesome Eyebot exposes both forms for the same "number of attacking creatures" wording once shared scalar comparisons are supported. Preserve the complete inner Zone subtree, including its kind, object filters, player/object references and binding IDs. Remove only the exact repeated Shared(Battlefield) membership test; do not simplify historical/observed sets, other zones, different filters or unknown operands. This normalization is owned by oracle-ir-contract and retains mapped ID origins. Native validation continues to reject extra fields. No information-policy, timing, holder, result-identity or AST schema change is introduced. See docs/grammar-simplification-20261113.md.

updates.summary: Limited Resources makes every player sacrifice their unselected lands, after all players have chosen.
updates.evidence: The Oracle entry trigger says "each player chooses five lands they control and sacrifices the rest". The pinned IR collects each player's choices with ForEachPlayer(All), but the following Sacrifice names only One(AbilityController). The sacrifice must act for All players, using the existing aggregate Unselected choice receipt. Preserve the two-instruction structure: all players choose before the sacrifice operation; do not move sacrifices inside the per-player choice loop. Only the sacrifice actor changes. The choice populations, controller filters, counts, result IDs and trigger subject remain unchanged. The owned AST already supports PlayerSet::All, so schema 190 remains unchanged. A regression checks the action order, aggregate receipt, actor set and printing an edited keep count. See docs/grammar-simplification-20261113.md.

updates.summary: An immediate sole-use capture and a pure Snapshot pump share the inline value form.
updates.evidence: Audit of the immutable allowed population found 10 faces that bind one deterministic scalar immediately before a Snapshot pump and use the result only in its power/toughness operands. Snapshot evaluates values as that instruction resolves; without an intervening action or another consumer, these captures have the same value and timing as inline expressions. Charix preserves the negative toughness operand; Raffine's Silencer preserves both negative operands and CurrentOrLastKnown information. Gloom Ripper and Monoist Circuit-Feeder are excluded because a second continuous effect also uses their captured values; Myr Battlesphere is excluded because its later damage reuses the captured quantity. Other reference pumps already inline the same kinds of counts/properties. Preserve every source, affected population, player/target identity, duration, remaining result ID, and complete expression subtree. Owned canonicalization checks every typed ResultId use, rejects nonlocal Affected/free Candidate references and unknown fields, and only handles pure single-change Snapshot pumps. It does not move captures across actions or normalize live evaluation, random/choice-dependent values, descendant Ability scopes, or expressions with result references. No lowering correction, information-policy change or AST schema change is introduced. See docs/grammar-simplification-20261113.md.

updates.summary: Phyrexian Ingester sums the current power and toughness of all linked creature cards in exile.
updates.evidence: The printed static ability defines X and Y using the same linked exiled creature-card population. The official Commander Masters release notes state that the bonuses use current power/toughness in exile, update when those values change, and give no bonus for a card that is not a creature in exile (https://magic.wizards.com/en/news/feature/commander-masters-release-notes). CR 607.3 requires summing variable answers when the linked exile ability has exiled multiple cards, such as from copied triggers (https://media.wizards.com/2026/downloads/MagicCompRules%2020260619.pdf). The old power operand chooses Query index zero from an unordered unfiltered linked population and cannot represent multiple linked cards; toughness uses a separate implicit Earlier(Exiled) measure. Replace both with Aggregate(Sum) over Zone(Shared(Exile),Card,AllOf(ExiledWith(Source),CardType(Creature))). Preserve the complete triggered exile ability, holder/source, affected object and static evaluation. This is an IR lowering/reference correction, not an equality alias: a first member and a whole population remain distinct. Existing AST types support the correction; no schema, model pin or reference lock change. See docs/grammar-simplification-20261113.md.

updates.summary: Creeping Inn counts creature cards among its linked exiled cards.
updates.evidence: The immutable allowed Oracle text explicitly defines X as the number of creature cards exiled with this creature. The seeded reference definition counts every linked card without a Creature predicate. Add CardType(Creature) to that same live Exile/Card population. Keep the complete payment, its strict movement selection and player, the conditional payment receipt, the BindValue capture after successful payment and before either life amount, both bound uses, and the independent phasing ability unchanged. This corrects an omitted written predicate; it is not an equality alias between filtered and unfiltered populations. Existing AST types support the corrected CountObjects filter. No model pin, reference lock or AST schema change. See docs/grammar-simplification-20261113.md.

updates.summary: A current all-player zone filtered to the ability controller's same zone uses that player scope directly.
updates.evidence: Audit of the immutable allowed reference found 495 exact current ObjectSet::Zone sites on 424 faces with Players(All) and either InZone(Players(One(AbilityController))) alone or exactly one same-zone membership term in AllOf. Intersecting all players' current instances of a zone with the controller's instance selects precisely that controller's zone. Move the intact One(AbilityController) scope into Zone and remove only that redundant InZone term. Preserve the zone name, object kind, every remaining filter and all containing operations, quantities, identities, histories and capture timing. Other same-zone membership clauses, different controllers, other player expressions, unknown fields and other selector types are excluded. The existing owned oracle-ir-contract canonical::narrow_zone_scope already defines this equality; no new alias, AST schema, model pin, reference lock, grammar rule or compiler rebuild is required. Old source operands are retained and validated through the native canonicalizer. See docs/grammar-simplification-20261113.md.

updates.summary: High Tide and Bubbling Muck give bonus mana to the player who tapped the land.
updates.evidence: The immutable allowed Oracle text says: Until end of turn, whenever a player taps an Island/a Swamp for mana, that player adds an additional mana of the named color. The CreateTrigger event records TapsForMana with players All. That player therefore refers to this event’s tapping player (PlayerRef::EventSubject), not to the controller of the spell or its delayed triggered ability (PlayerRef::AbilityController). The seeded m_until_end_of_turn_event_clause_that_player hardcoded the latter. Replace only the AddMana player leaf; preserve the delayed event, its filter, duration, announcement, results, mana color and quantity. The shared scoped trigger grammar already binds the written player correctly. Existing AST types suffice; no schema, model pin or reference lock change. This is a semantic correction, not a canonicalization alias between the two player identities. See docs/grammar-simplification-20261113.md.

updates.summary: Yurlok’s unobserved fixed universal mana action uses one AddMana(All) instruction.
updates.evidence: The allowed immutable Oracle text says Each player adds {B}{R}{G}. Native Instruction::ForEachPlayer specifies simultaneous actions after APNAP choices (CR 101.4). This body has only one unrestricted fixed literal mana production, with its recipient exactly the loop-bound player and no choice, dynamic amount, ordering directive or result observer. It has the same meaning as one AddMana with players All and the unchanged complete mana bundle. The owned canonicalizer now proves this narrow reduction using bounded typed lossless matching, lexical binding and whole-ability result-use checks, including future programs. It preserves the moved child effect’s result and provenance, and rejects invalid duplicate bindings, extra operands and forged origin metadata. Replace the loop instruction with its child AddMana addressing All; preserve all other abilities, costs, filters, quantities and result identities. Both native forms validate and canonicalize to the same meaning; this is not an alias for arbitrary player loops, choice-bearing or dynamic mana, restrictions, ordering or observed receipts. No AST type/schema, model pin or reference-lock change. See SPEC.md and docs/grammar-simplification-20261113.md.

updates.summary: Positive fixed literal mana in one production uses canonical totals by color.
updates.evidence: ManaProduction::All explicitly describes one production, not independent productions. A bundle containing only positive Constant amounts of White, Blue, Black, Red, Green or Colorless mana has the same colors and total units whether represented by repeated units, nested literal All bundles or one amount per color. The owned canonicalizer now merges these pure literal totals with checked i64 arithmetic and a fixed color order. Zero amounts, chosen colors, choices, dynamic expressions, empty bundles, overflow and unknown fields are excluded. This bounded typed normalization preserves all recipients, instructions, restrictions, receipt IDs and their observers, as well as every nonliteral production. The recursive literal-mana grammar’s inverse removes one current unit at a time and enumerates every available first color, preserving exact keyed orders without relying on saved wording. Change only schema-typed ManaProduction roots identified through the owned frozen schema 190; do not inspect or rewrite opaque metadata. Each replacement includes only literal-bundle normalization inside that same production. Existing AST types suffice; no schema, model pin or reference-lock change. See SPEC.md and docs/grammar-simplification-20261113.md.

updates.summary: Alternative casting restrictions use one CastSpell predicate with alternative object filters.
updates.evidence: The Ringhart Crest says "cast a creature spell of the chosen type or a legendary creature spell". Its pinned reference uses ManaUse::Either of two CastSpell predicates; Volshe Tideturner expresses "cast an instant or sorcery spell or a kicked spell" as one CastSpell with ObjectFilter::AnyOf. Both test the same payment action against alternative spell filters. Normalize only nonempty Either nodes whose every arm is exactly CastSpell. Preserve every entire filter and all typed references, including source, chosen type and target identity. The owned typed canonicalizer performs the same reduction after visiting children, without revisiting or renumbering their IDs. Other payment actions, mixed alternatives, conjunctions, negation, source-domain flags, conditions, spending changes and invalid extra fields are not merged. The complete allowed pinned reference was scanned only at schema-190 ManaUse sites, with opaque metadata excluded; this is the sole matching face. Existing AST types suffice; no model schema, pin or reference-lock change. This is equivalent-shape normalization, not a semantic correction. See SPEC.md and docs/grammar-simplification-20261113.md.

updates.summary: Damage-prevention shields preserve the written damage source and recipient direction.
updates.evidence: Repository issue #4 reports nine reversed prevention events in pinned schema-190 records. Balduvian Hydra, Ethereal Champion, Opal-Eye Konda's Yojimbo, Ordruun Commando, Rasputin Dreamweaver, Revered Elder, Rock Hydra and Ursine Fylgja prevent damage dealt TO the named creature; retain arbitrary damage sources and match that creature as recipient. Barbed Wire instead prevents damage dealt BY that artifact; restrict the source to that same permanent and allow every recipient. Preserve the amount, duration, limit, event kind/grouping/subject, costs, controller and replacement body. The current grammar's seeded meanings contain the same reversal and are corrected alongside these records; this is a semantic correction, not an equality normalization. Existing AST types suffice. Issue: https://github.com/vishvananda/oracle-grammar/issues/4 . Upstream repair evidence: https://github.com/vishvananda/mtgish/commit/91a2fe43 . The local regression family checks each corrected native event and rejects the old readings. See docs/reported-issues-20261113.md.

updates.summary: Gauntlets of Chaos destroys only attached Auras after its successful exchange.
updates.evidence: Repository issue #5: the Oracle sentence says destroy all Auras attached to the exchanged permanents. The reference matches either attachment target but omits Subtype(Aura), so attached Equipment is incorrectly included. Conjoin the existing complete attachment disjunction with the Aura subtype, preserving both target slots, the exchange-success guard, cost, ordering and destruction regeneration flag. Do not replace the disjunction or widen the subtype test. This corrects one typed filter operand and the matching seeded grammar declaration; no AST schema change or equality alias. Upstream repair evidence: https://github.com/vishvananda/mtgish/commit/855deccc . See https://github.com/vishvananda/oracle-grammar/issues/5 and docs/reported-issues-20261113.md.

updates.summary: Mercenaries prevention matches damage from that creature to the activating player.
updates.evidence: Repository issue #6: the next-time shield names both this creature and you. The reference retains AbilityController as recipient but has Any source, allowing unrelated damage to consume the shield. Restrict sources to SameObject(Source) in the Permanent source domain. Preserve the activating player identity, Any-player activation permission, NextOccurrence limit, duration, cost and replacement body. Correct the matching grammar declaration with the same complete event predicate. This is a semantic correction using existing AST operands, not a source/controller alias or schema change. Upstream repair evidence: https://github.com/vishvananda/mtgish/commit/4ba5c00f . See https://github.com/vishvananda/oracle-grammar/issues/6 and docs/reported-issues-20261113.md.

updates.summary: Your next untap step retains the ability controller as both step player and expiration player.
updates.evidence: Repository issue #8 identifies 17 controller-following durations on explicitly named your-next-untap wording. Correct both DuringNextUntapStep(AbilityController) and UntapStep.players=One(AbilityController), preserving affected objects, activation/trigger identity, other changes, source, ordering and LiveObjects evaluation. Correcting only the lifetime would still let the step predicate follow a different controller, including off-turn untaps. Barl's Cage's explicit controller-following wording and Orcish Farmer's distinct controller reference remain unchanged controls. The original 17 faces are all in the explicit allowed population. These are semantic operand corrections, without a schema change or identity alias. See https://github.com/vishvananda/oracle-grammar/issues/8 , published upstream repair https://github.com/vishvananda/mtgish/commit/7fed1a80affa9e6ed5067210333243e3c3ada4b5 and docs/reported-issues-20261113.md.

updates.summary: Live untap rules on a population controlled by the ability controller use that stable player role explicitly.
updates.evidence: The same allowed wording audit also finds five land effects whose duration already names AbilityController and whose LiveObjects battlefield population is explicitly constrained by ControlledBy(One(AbilityController)). Every affected object therefore has that controller whenever the live rule applies. Its UntapStep player predicate ControllerOf(Affected) is equivalent, in precisely that proven context, to AbilityController. Normalize that predicate to the same stable named-player shape used for the other your-next-untap rules. The owned typed canonicalizer proves only this literal AbilityController implication on an exact current battlefield Zone, an explicit conjunct or whole ControlledBy predicate, one Skip rule, LiveObjects evaluation and DuringNextUntapStep(AbilityController); it bounds conjunction inspection and preserves unknown fields. It does not alias players on fixed/snapshot or unfiltered populations, change a controller-following duration, accept another player/window, or broaden the 17 actual corrections. Both replaced roles are ID-free, so no typed reference origin is removed or synthesized. Existing AST types suffice. See docs/reported-issues-20261113.md.

updates.summary: Juxtapose performs its independent creature and artifact exchanges in printed order.
updates.evidence: Repository issue #7: the pinned spell contains only two creature choices and their exchange. Append the independent artifact choices and exchange, preserving the first exchange, each player as chooser, maximum-mana-value eligibility, as-many-as-possible count and each exchange's separate result references. The artifact sequence is unconditional after the creature sequence, so failure or absence of the creature exchange does not suppress it. Generic shared grammar emits both complete exchanges from their current permanent kinds and player; the three former fragments that incorrectly distributed one exchange over all three printed sentences are removed. Existing AST types suffice. Published upstream witness/repair: https://github.com/vishvananda/mtgish/commit/4ba5c00f6e5a1b5f32abf8e017a10ccf74bd9fff . See https://github.com/vishvananda/oracle-grammar/issues/7 and docs/reported-issues-20261113.md.

updates.summary: Vexing Arcanix guards both name branches by an actual reveal and moves that observed card.
updates.evidence: Repository issue #10: an empty library still permits the prior naming choice, but provides no card for either name-comparison branch. Wrap the entire original name-test If in CountObjects(Observed(reveal_result)) >= 1, with an empty otherwise program. Naming and revealing remain outside the guard. Both moves refer to that actual Observed receipt instead of freshly querying the top library card, retaining the revealed object identity. The wrong-name damage therefore cannot occur when no card was revealed. Preserve costs, target player, name-choice domain, move destinations, source, amount and existing result IDs. This is a semantic/identity correction without an AST schema change. Published upstream repair/witnesses: https://github.com/vishvananda/mtgish/commit/06de9c786d700414985cb9cf960402169039b830 . See https://github.com/vishvananda/oracle-grammar/issues/10 and docs/reported-issues-20261113.md.

updates.summary: Maelstrom Archangel Avatar iterates distinct damage-time creature sources instead of the current battlefield.
updates.evidence: Repository issue #14 and upstream contract clarification #125: creature/controller predicates apply when combat damage was dealt to a player this turn. Replace the current Battlefield population with Union([FromHistory(Damage{source_kind:Permanent,sources:Creature AND ControlledBy(AbilityController),recipients:Players(All),kind:Combat,grouping:Source,subject:Source},ThisTurn)]). The set union deduplicates repeated events for the same source identity. Departed creatures and later control changes cannot alter which historical participants qualify. Preserve loop binding, mana-COST matching (not mana value), random selection, copy operations, optional payment and all result identities. No schema change or source/current-controller equality alias. Published corrected lowering and scoped regressions: https://github.com/vishvananda/mtgish/commit/123fb91240db27e8396a24bd10274ce9d1618183 . See https://github.com/vishvananda/oracle-grammar/issues/14 and docs/reported-issues-20261113.md.

updates.summary: Maelstrom Archangel Avatar tests both printed chosen-copy types explicitly.
updates.evidence: While correcting issue #14, the same pinned body was found to lower two positive printed conditions into one If/else: any failure of the permanent test offered the spell-casting branch, including when no copy was chosen. Preserve the permanent then-program with an empty otherwise, and add the explicit Instant OR Sorcery chosen-copy condition with the original casting program and an empty otherwise. Both printed conditions now retain their own meanings; no missing/other-kind copy falls into an unconditional cast branch. Keep optional payment and choice ordering, actor, copy identities, result IDs and all body operands. The grammar also fixes formerly unrepresented count words to the actual single-copy wording and checks agreement between the loop noun and its repeated noun; edited costs and loop kinds still derive from current operands. This is a semantic lowering correction using existing AST types, not an equivalence normalization. See docs/reported-issues-20261113.md and https://github.com/vishvananda/oracle-grammar/issues/14 .

updates.summary: Direct least-power destruction chooses a destructible member of the already computed minimum pool.
updates.evidence: Repository issue #12: Drop of Honey and Porphyry Nodes instruct destruction directly, so CR609.3 requires doing as much as possible. Preserve the complete existing creature/minimum-power population, then apply Not(HasKeyword(Indestructible)) outside that population before selecting. Do not filter the Aggregate Minimum input: an indestructible least-power creature must not make a higher-power creature eligible. Preserve the controller chooser, AsManyAsCan(1), result addresses and no-regeneration destruction. Imperial Edict's separate choose instruction remains unrestricted by this direct-destruction legality filter. Published primary lowering/runtime-witness evidence: https://github.com/vishvananda/mtgish/commit/2e6c5d6008fe90c72da86393e56f568a2a43f492 . See https://github.com/vishvananda/oracle-grammar/issues/12 and docs/reported-issues-20261113.md. Existing AST types suffice.

updates.summary: Frankenstein's Monster performs an as-much-as-possible exile effect and checks actual exile arrivals.
updates.evidence: Repository issue #13: the entering instruction is an effect governed by CR609.3, not an indivisible cost under CR118.3. Replace mandatory PayCost(Move Exactly X) with WithSelections choosing AsManyAsCan(X), followed by the actual exile Move. Compare the number of actual After transitions arriving in Exile to the entering object's CastX; if incomplete, retain the original owner-graveyard entry redirect. The counter amount counts actual creature-card arrivals in the same receipt. Use Matching(Transition{After},InZone(Exile)) on the recorded arrival incarnation, not ObjectSet::InZone current membership, not requested inputs and not a fresh zone query. Redirected arrivals do not count, while later movement cannot erase a recorded exile arrival. Preserve the entering controller, selection population, counter kinds/choice semantics, destinations and instruction identities; real costs are unchanged. Existing schema-190 types suffice. Published primary repairs/witnesses: https://github.com/vishvananda/mtgish/commit/2e6c5d6008fe90c72da86393e56f568a2a43f492 and https://github.com/vishvananda/mtgish/commit/9ffdb82199daa30db62113eeb2ab42b0cef5ea85 . See https://github.com/vishvananda/oracle-grammar/issues/13 and docs/reported-issues-20261113.md.

updates.summary: Post-destroy characteristic tests retain the original target independently of successful destruction.
updates.evidence: Repository issue #9: Thermokarst and Extinguish the Light test the targeted permanent even when destruction fails. Replace the successful-destroy Result{Before,index0} condition operand with the actual Target reference from the preceding instruction, retaining its current/last-known identity, filter, comparison, reward and all other operands. The shared grammar had an incorrect comment/meaning treating a performed-action Before receipt as attempted input; it now repeats the captured target explicitly instead. This is a semantic identity correction, not a Result/Target equality alias. No schema change. Published upstream repair/witnesses: https://github.com/vishvananda/mtgish/commit/06de9c786d700414985cb9cf960402169039b830 . See https://github.com/vishvananda/oracle-grammar/issues/9 and docs/reported-issues-20261113.md.
